transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-02 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Noah (Redwood); Priya, Carlos, Sofia, Evan (Asterion)
Links referenced: onboarding runbook: https://redwood.example/onboarding-runbook, security pack: https://redwood.example/security-pack, SLA deck: https://redwood.example/sla-deck

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Chen, AE for Redwood. Quick mic check?
[00:12] Priya: Hi Maya, Priya here — loud and clear. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:18] Maya: Awesome. I'll hand to Liam for a quick technical orientation and then we'll go through your success criteria.
[00:22] Liam: Yeah thanks. Hi all, Liam Patel, solutions engineer. Quick agenda: goals, topology (VPC vs hosted), data flows, security requirements, and an ops runbook overview.
[00:35] Evan: Sounds good. We have a hard Q1 goal to ship a triage assistant for clinicians, so timeline is tight — early March pilot.
[00:45] Maya: Noted. Priya, can you walk us through the top success metrics?
[00:52] Priya: Sure. Top things: latency under 300ms p95 for short prompts, privacy of PHI in logs, and cost target — we need to keep inference cost below $0.004 per 1k tokens for the clinical flows. Also, model hallucination rate should be auditable.
[01:12] Liam: Okay latency at 300ms p95 will push us toward Dedicated with local region routing; Hosted can hit it for small scale but may be variable. On cost, we'll look at batching/quantization profiles.
[01:33] Carlos: Can you explain the Dedicated option again? We're worried about operational burden.
[01:40] Liam: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for your tenant with predictable throughput. Redwood manages the runtime; you get isolated capacity, VPC peering, and optional private control plane. There is a small ops runway to configure networking but Redwood ops helps with the setup.
[01:56] Sofia: From compliance, we need to verify SOC two artifacts, S S O / SAML integration, and K M S key management for encryption at rest. Also audit logs for every token request.
[02:12] Noah: Yep, we have a SOC2 pack in the security link I posted. We support SAML SSO and can integrate with your KMS or use Redwood-managed keys with HSM. Audit logs are available per-request in the console; retention is configurable.
[02:30] Priya: For PHI, can logs be turned off for certain routes or scrubbed?
[02:37] Liam: We have a KV/prefix cache approach and you can opt-out of storing full request bodies. There's a 'no-logs' mode for endpoints handling PHI; we'll document tradeoffs for debugging vs privacy.
[02:50] Carlos: Network constraints: we run in an air-gapped segment but can open peering to trusted subnets. We'll share IP ranges. Any gotchas on peering?
[02:59] Liam: We'll need CIDR ranges, BGP details if you want dynamic routes, and a couple minutes of firewall rules. For dedicated in your region we'll do VPC peering or private link.
[03:18] Priya: Great. On evaluation: we want to run a 2-week benchmark window with our prompts to measure latency and cost.
[03:25] Maya: Totally — recommended path is: 1) small dedicated pool provisioned for the 2-week window, 2) your team runs sample traffic, 3) Redwood runs profiling and suggests batching/quantization.
[03:40] Evan: What's the approximate cost of a short dedicated pilot?
[03:44] Maya: Rough order: one reserved slot for two weeks ranges depending on GPU type — we'll send concrete pricing. For planning assume $Xk for the pilot; we'll give exact numbers in the follow-up sheet.
[03:56] Sofia: We'll need contractual language about PHI handling. Do you have BAAs or any healthcare addendum?
[04:04] Maya: Redwood supports BAAs as an add-on for Private deployments; for Hosted we have stricter controls and can provide a healthcare addendum under enterprise contracts. I'll flag legal.
[04:20] Priya: On integration, we plan to call Redwood API from our inference gateway; do you support streaming and function calling?
[04:29] Liam: Yes, streaming and structured outputs are supported; function-calling style responses are supported too. For production we recommend KV cache for repetitive context to reduce tokens.
[04:45] Carlos: About KV cache — is it tenant-isolated? And how long is it retained?
[04:51] Liam: Tenant-isolated, and TTLs are configurable per-route. You can also configure prefix caching vs full session cache.
[04:59] Priya: Any limitations around quantized models for clinical language? We don't want accuracy regressions.
[05:07] Liam: We'll recommend quant profiles by workload; we run small evals to detect ROUGE/EM decline thresholds. For critical flows we recommend evaluation before switching to higher quant levels.
[05:22] Maya: Quick check from Priya: how do you define success for the pilot?
[05:27] Priya: Three things: meeting latency & cost targets, no PHI leakage in logs, and model output quality within our baseline eval (we'll share eval prompts).
[05:38] Maya: Perfect. We'll add those as acceptance criteria in the runbook.
[05:44] Carlos: Role permissions — we need RBAC so only certain users can view logs and export tokens.
[05:50] Noah: Redwood Console supports role-based access with customizable roles; SSO provisioning via SAML or SCIM.
[05:59] Sofia: How do you handle key rotation for K M S?
[06:03] Liam: We support customer-managed keys with automatic rotation or you can rotate manually via your KMS. We'll document the flow.
[06:12] Evan: Timeline recap: Pilot start target 2026-02-16, two-week window, ship pilot improvements by early March. Is that feasible?
[06:22] Maya: Yes that aligns. Action owners and dates we'll capture.
[06:28] Priya: One more — data residency: can you pin to US-East only?
[06:33] Liam: Yes regions can be pinned; for Dedicated we'll provision in the region you select.
[06:39] Carlos: Ok we'll share VPC contact and the allowlist today.
[06:44] Sofia: And I'll collate SOC2 doc requests and send them to Maya.
[06:49] Maya: Great. Any blockers around procurement?
[06:53] Priya: Procurement needs a scoping doc and a rough TCO for the pilot to get approval; can you provide?
[06:58] Maya: We'll send a one-page scoping + TCO.
[07:02] Evan: For the pilot we'll need quick access to the console for a few of our engineers. How long to provision?
[07:07] Noah: Once we have the CRM/setup approvals, console accounts can be provisioned in under 24 hours; Dedicated infra provisioning is longer — usually 3–5 business days.
[07:20] Maya: Ok let's open the floor for any technical deep dive points — Carlos?
[07:24] Carlos: Just to confirm metrics we'll surface in the dashboard: per-route latency, token counts, cost per route, and errors?
[07:31] Liam: Yep, per-route breakouts, token-level cost, and trace IDs for request-level debugging. We can also wire up export to your observability stack.
[07:42] Priya: Keep an eye on hallucination monitoring — do you have eval hooks?
[07:47] Liam: We do — Redwood Optimize supports eval trigger sets and regression alerts.
[07:52] Maya: Alright, recap and owners: I'll send the onboarding runbook and SLA deck by 2/5, Liam will schedule security deep dive with Sofia, ops will provision the pilot capacity for 2/16, Carlos will share VPC details by 2/6, Sofia will send SOC2 artifacts list by 2/10. Any objections?
[08:12] Priya: None, that works.
[08:16] Maya: Thank you all. We'll follow up with meeting notes and a calendar invite for the security deep dive.
[08:22] Evan: Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-attributions and transcription errors expected (e.g., 'K V cache' vs 'KV cache', 'S O C two' vs 'SOC2'). End of transcript.
